{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Malaysia|Cuisine of Malaysia]]

'''Bah kut teh''' (literally, "spare rib tea") is a Hokkien specialty. It is an exotic herbal soup spiced with plenty of aromatic spices including [[Cookbook:Star Anise|star anise]], [[Cookbook:Cinnamon|cinnamon]], cloves and lots of [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]]. It is often served with Chinese doughnuts and goes well with white rice. It usually comes with a small serve of cut red chillies in dark soy sauce or garlic.

==Ingredients==

* 6 dried [[Cookbook:Mushroom|shitake mushrooms]]
* 1½ [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]] (680 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) [[Cookbook:Pork|pork spareribs]], cut into 2-[[Cookbook:Inch|inch]] (5 cm) pieces
* 1 whole bulb [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]], unpeeled and slightly crushed
* 2 inches (5 cm) [[Cookbook:Chinese Herbs|ginseng root]], peeled and slightly crushed
* 3 [[Cookbook:Cinnamon|cinnamon]] sticks
* 5 [[Cookbook:Star Anise|star anise]] pods
* 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Pepper|white peppercorns]]
* 1 tbsp [[Cookbook:Pepper|black peppercorns]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
* 1 tbsp [[Cookbook:Soy Sauce|dark soy sauce]]
* 6 [[Cookbook:Shallot|shallots]], finely [[Cookbook:Slicing|sliced]] and fried until golden brown (optional)
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]]
* [[Cookbook:Pepper|Pepper]]

==Procedure==
# Soak dried shitake mushrooms in 240 ml [[Cookbook:Boiling|boiling]] water to reconstitute. Slice into strips when soft; reserve liquid for cooking.
# In a stockpot, cover spareribs with cold water, then [[Cookbook:Parboil|parboil]] ribs until froth rises to the surface.
# Drain, briefly rinse spareribs under cold running water, and drain again.
# In a casserole pan add the parboiled spare ribs, garlic bulb, ginseng root, shitake mushrooms, reserved liquid and additional water (to cover the meat).
# Wrap cinnamon, star anise, white and black peppercorns in [[Cookbook:Cheesecloth|cheesecloth]], tie with string, and add to the pan.
# Gradually bring to a boil, then cover and reduce heat to [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] until pork is very tender (about 45–60 minutes); occasionally skim off fat from the surface.
# When the meat is almost falling off the bones; discard spice bag, season with salt and pepper and add dark soy sauce and sugar.
